title: The cache-aside TTL bounds LOCAL staleness; the guide names KV vendor propagation as a separate clock
asA: developer reading platform-cloudflare-kv guidance about cache-aside expiry versus KV eventual consistency
iWant: the guide to separate the applied cache-aside TTL (local expiry) from the vendor-owned KV propagation window (global read visibility) so I do not misread the TTL as a global staleness ceiling
soThat: when the applied project asserts a 60-second TTL, I know it bounds local re-fetch cadence only, not the moment every other network location observes the write

acceptanceCriteria.description: The cache-aside helper's local expiry window matches the elicited TTL exactly: driven with a fake clock, a read that lands within elicitedTtlMs of the write returns the cached value with source cache; a read at elicitedTtlMs+1 re-invokes originFn and returns source origin. The two events (kvHit before the expiry boundary, kvMiss after) emit in that causal order on the sink; no cross-region KV propagation timing is asserted by this AC because the vendor documents that clock at 60 seconds or more and it is not a mechanism the applied project owns.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a cache-aside helper wired against an in-memory KV driver and a fake clock, with the elicited TTL set to 60000ms
acceptanceCriteria.when: sequential reads land at 59_000ms and 61_000ms after a warmed write
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first read returns source cache (kvHit), the second returns source origin (kvMiss), and no cross-region propagation claim is made

acceptanceCriteria.description: The guide passage on eventual consistency names the KV propagation window (up to 60 seconds or more per the Cloudflare KV documented behaviour) as a separate clock from the applied cache-aside TTL; a doc-string test greps guide.md for the phrase "separate clock" and for the decision-tree cross-reference to platform-cloudflare-durable-objects (round-6 T-3) as the strong-consistency answer.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the shipped guide file at guide/platform-cloudflare-kv.md
acceptanceCriteria.when: a doc-string test greps the guide for the required phrases
acceptanceCriteria.then: both phrases are present and the guide names DO as the strong-consistency answer
